messages.author: Matthew Guberman-Pfeffer
messages.body:
Dear AMBER community,
I am trying to install AMBER, first the serial version, and ultimately the GPU-enalbed version.
I’m trying to do the installation on my account at the PSC (I was told each user has to install it for his/herself), but I’m having trouble. Below is the issue:
The provided instructions say "mdgx was giving an error message and it is no longer used, so, in
the run.cmake add -DDISABLE_TOOLS=“mdgx”
I found run_cmake, not run.cmake. Assuming it’s the same file, I added -DDISABLE_TOOLS=“mdgx”, but cmake complained:
Parse error in command line argument: -DDISABLE_TOOLS
Should be: VAR:type=value
CMake Error: No cmake script provided.
CMake Error: Problem processing arguments. Aborting.
If I omit -DDISABLE_TOOLS, cmake works, and the following installation looks fine, but when I run the tests, I get the below errors:
possible FAILURE: check bis_2.out.dif
possible FAILURE: check spc.xvv.other.dif
possible FAILURE: (ignored) check /jet/home/mag14011/amber22/AmberTools/src/FEW/examples/test/calc_a_1t/AMT/pqr_snaps/AMT_rec.pqr.3.dif
possible FAILURE: check nve.out.dif
possible FAILURE: (ignored) check min.out.dif
These tests don’t appear to have anything to do with mdgx unless I’m mistaken. How can I resolve these (possible) failures? I don’t know what they mean.
Ultimately, I want to install the GPU enabled version. I’d appreciate any help getting that done to move my research forward!
Best,
Matthew

What is the reference for the instructions you are following ?
Presumably these are not the ones in the Amber manual.
run_cmake is indeed the Amber documented place to start;
see ambermd.org/Manuals.php
Your cmake problem is due to the use of quotes since this worked for me:
-DDISABLE_TOOLS=mdgx
.
.
.
-- NOT Building Tools:
...
-- mdgx - Disabled by user
-- **************************************************************************
To check the possible failures, see the files under amber22/logs
The installation section of our manual also has advice on checking
the tests.
scott

messages.author: David A Case
messages.body:
On Wed, Nov 09, 2022, Matthew Guberman-Pfeffer via AMBER wrote:
>
>
>I found run_cmake, not run.cmake. Assuming it’s the same file, I added
>-DDISABLE_TOOLS=“mdgx”, but cmake complained:
>
>Parse error in command line argument: -DDISABLE_TOOLS
>Should be: VAR:type=value
>CMake Error: No cmake script provided.
Sounds like you didn't add the -DDISABLE_TOOLS in the proper way. It is not
a command-line argument, but you put it inside the run_cmake script itself.
>If I omit -DDISABLE_TOOLS, cmake works, and the following installation
>looks fine,
Is mdgx built with this run?
> but when I run the tests, I get the below errors:
>
>possible FAILURE: check bis_2.out.dif
>possible FAILURE: check spc.xvv.other.dif
>possible FAILURE: check nve.out.dif
Look at nve.out.dif and the other: do the errors look serious? It may be
that you won't have to worry about these errors.
>
.....dac

messages.author: James Kress
messages.body:
Using Amber 22 on a RHEL 8 system. I had to go from RHEL 8.4 to 8.8 and
CUDA toolkit 11.4 to 11.8 due to a server malfunction.
Do I need to recompile Amber and amber tools or can I use the executables
generate previously?
Thanks for any assistance.
Jim Kress
-----Original Message-----
From: Matthew Guberman-Pfeffer via AMBER <amber.ambermd.org>
Sent: Thursday, November 10, 2022 9:07 AM
To: David A Case <david.case.rutgers.edu>
Cc: AMBER Mailing List <amber.ambermd.org>
Subject: Re: [AMBER] Installation Problem
Dr. Case, the diff value is attached.
What do you think about the seriousness?
Yes, I think mdgx was built. I can try next to use the flag correctly
(without quotes) like Scott suggested.

messages.author: Scott Brozell
messages.body:
Hi,
Yes.
(There are a lot of if ands or buts; however, the simplest way to
guarantee that the new toolkit is used is to rebuild after running
clean_build
)
scott
